set_text.text: Landed cost is what a product costs you at your dock: the supplier's price plus the freight and fees to get it there. Split per unit, it lets you compare supplier offers that come in different case sizes. It is the number to rank on, not the quoted price.
The case price plus freight per case, split across the units inside. Option C's $19.00 case lands at $20.20, which is $2.02 a unit.
The cost of holding what you bought. A 24 unit case can win on landed cost and still tie up more cash and warehouse space while it sells through.
A backhaul still has a freight cost
If your own truck collects the order on a return trip, freight is not zero. Put your truck's cost for that stop in the freight box, split down to the case.
Who uses a landed cost calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who buy the same item from more than one supplier. Anyone who signs off on a supplier switch should see the per unit ranking first.
